FXUS65 KPUB 271137
AFDPUB

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Pueblo CO
537 AM MDT Thu Aug 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- One more day of scattered to numerous showers and
  thunderstorms across the area today, with a flash flood risk
  for the Aspen Acres burn scar, and one or two severe storms
  possible along I-25.  

- Drier and warmer on Friday, with mainly isolated mountain 
  showers and storms. 

- Thunderstorm chances will increase this weekend and into next
  week, especially over the mountains, as deeper moisture 
  returns to the mainly the western half of Colorado.

&&

.SHORT TERM /THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Issued at 1236 AM MDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Usual lingering convection over the far eastern plains early 
this morning, and again expect most activity to end or shift
into KS well before sunrise. Expect one last round of fairly
widespread mountain convection this afternoon as
moisture/instability remain in place, with storms pushing into 
the I-25 corridor during the late afternoon and evening. Eastern
mountains look most susceptible to stronger storms and heavy 
rain, with a low threat of a severe storm or two along I-25 
where modest 0-6km shear(20-30 kts) and CAPE(1000-1200 J/KG) 
coincide. Models show only a few weakening storms drifting east
of I-25 in the evening, as best forcing for storms on the 
plains will be well north in nern CO/wrn NE. Flash Flood Watch 
looks good for the Aspen Acres again today, though just like 
yesterday, ultimate location and magnitude of any flooding will 
depend on difficult to forecast mesoscale/convective details. 

Upper ridge flattens slightly Fri afternoon, with mid level wly
flow bringing in at least a temporarily drier air mass to the
region. Low/mid flow on the plains turns more wly as well, with
deepening lee trough east of I-25. Expect a substantial downturn
in convective strength and coverage Friday as a result, though 
isolated mountain storms will remain possible from mid- 
afternoon into early evening. Max temps will respond to general 
wly downslope flow, with maxes back into the 90s on the plains, 
with 80s most interior valleys and mountains.

&&

.LONG TERM /FRIDAY NIGHT THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1236 AM MDT Thu Aug 27 2026

SW flow aloft strengthens across CO on Sat, as center of the
upper level high drifts back eastward into TX. Renewed tap of 
mid-level moisture will work into the state by late Sat
afternoon, and with weak s/w trough moving across, expect fairly
widespread showers and storms to return to the mountains,
especially along the Continental Divide. Swly steering flow 
will take a few storms into the I-25 corridor Sat evening, while
the plains stay mainly dry, as breezy sw surface winds behind 
the lee trough in wrn KS aren't particularly helpful in keeping 
activity going away from the higher terrain. Deep mixing Sat 
will squeeze a couple more degf out of the air mass, with maxes 
into the 90s on the plains (a few 100f readings in the lower 
Arkansas Valley), and 80s mountains and valleys. Strong upper 
wave then races eastward through the nrn Rockies Sun/Mon, with 
surface cold front dropping through the area late Sun/early Mon.
Mid level moisture will continue to flow across the state both 
Sun/Mon, with widespread showers and thunderstorms over the 
mountains both days, lesser chances on the plains. Still hot on 
Sun ahead of the front, then slightly cooler Mon/Tue behind it. 
Precip chances may then decrease slightly Tue/Wed as main
moisture tap shifts back west of Colorado, though moisture 
never goes away completely, so isolated afternoon/evening 
showers and thunderstorms will persist, especially over the 
mountains back toward the Continental Divide.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 537 AM MDT Thu Aug 27 2026

VFR conditions anticipated across much of the forecast area over the 
next 24 hrs, including the three main TAF sites of KCOS, KPUB and 
KALS. Convection will develop across the higher terrain by 18z 
today, affecting TAF sites by mid-afternoon. Therefore, introduced 
PROB30 wording for all three sites by 22z and lasting through 02z 
for KALS, AND 03Z for KCOS/KPUB, for variable wind gusts to 30-35 
kts and -TSRA. Strong to severe thunderstorms will be possible 
through the afternoon and evening along the eastern mts and I-25 
Corridor, potentially affecting KCOS and KPUB, with the main threats 
being damaging wind gusts and hail 1 inch in diameter. 

&&

.PUB WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Flash Flood Watch from 1 PM MDT this afternoon through this 
evening for COZ079-080-086.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...PETERSEN
LONG TERM...PETERSEN
AVIATION...MOORE
